effectiveContext.name: Significant Astro UI implementation profile v2
effectiveContext.selectionRule: Full files initially required or directly routed for an Astro UI task with page-specific styling, accessibility, and explicit bundle-isolation requirements. Matching design-system inventory entries and implementation sources are queried later and are not represented as whole loaded files.

overallSummary: The significant Astro UI profile now routes directly to the documentation and skills needed for the declared work, keeps workflow and review references conditional, and gives exact package commands one authoritative source. The remaining precision cost is within the broad performance playbook: bundle-isolation guidance is required for this profile, but several media and third-party sections are not.
strengths: AGENTS.md explicitly distinguishes coding-agent authority from human-facing documentation and names source-of-truth files.
Task routing exposes architecture, design-system, accessibility, performance, Storybook, specification, and Context Health entry points without loading unrelated routes by default.
Only the safe-change skill is universal for implementation; Astro, performance, UI, search, SEO, Context Health, and copy-edit skills are conditional.
Package scripts remain authoritative, while the agent documentation validator checks routed links, heading anchors, and documented script names.

priorities.finding: The performance skill is correctly routed for this profile's bundle-isolation requirement, but loading the whole file also includes media, font, analytics, and third-party guidance that the declared task may not use.
priorities.recommendation: Keep the current route until repeated audits justify smaller performance playbooks; when loading the full skill, assess its unrelated sections as a Context Precision cost.

metrics.label: Context Precision
metrics.interpretation: The loaded files are task-relevant and directly routed; the broad performance playbook contains the profile's required isolation guidance alongside unrelated media and third-party checks.

checks.label: Change types route to focused documentation
checks.interpretation: The routing rules load matching documentation by default and explicitly keep unrelated routes out of initial context.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md tells agents to select applicable task rows, records when extra context expands scope, forbids score gaming, and maps distinct change types to separate references.

checks.label: Loaded UI guidance is precise within each file
checks.interpretation: The Astro, accessibility, and CSS skills are tightly relevant, but the required performance skill includes several sections outside this profile's bundle-isolation need.

evidence.observation: The selected skills cover static rendering, native semantics, focus, contrast, token-based styles, and bundle isolation; the performance file also includes image, media, font, analytics, and third-party-resource checks.

checks.label: Always-required skills stay narrow for all implementation tasks
checks.interpretation: Only the safe-change skill is universal; all technical, UI, search, SEO, prose, and Context Health skills are routed by matching task scope.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md requires agent-safe-change for implementation and places every other skill in a task-to-skill table.

checks.label: Repeated command summaries avoid redundant context
checks.interpretation: The authority file keeps a small validation summary, the README keeps a human quick start, and testing documentation owns the complete check guidance.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md names package.json as exact authority and points to testing guidance; README lists five primary commands; docs/testing.md contains the full validation reference.

metrics.label: Context Recall
metrics.interpretation: The authority file directly exposes the major task routes, matching specifications, Storybook guidance, design-system sources, and conditional skills required by this profile.

checks.label: Major change areas are routed from the authority file
checks.interpretation: The authority file exposes the principal documentation entry points needed for repository changes.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md directly lists task-specific documentation routes and a separate change-to-validation table.

checks.label: Feature specifications are directly discoverable
checks.interpretation: Agents can discover a referenced specification directly from the authority file and are told to load only the matching file.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md directly routes tasks that mention a feature, plan, specification, or prior decision to matching filenames under specs and says not to load the directory as a corpus.

checks.label: Storybook work has a direct canonical route
checks.interpretation: Story work reaches one testing section that owns source locations, commands, deployment behavior, and production isolation.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md directly routes Storybook tasks to docs/testing.md, which identifies configuration and story locations, commands, deployment path, and isolation.

checks.label: Design-system guidance is discoverable
checks.interpretation: Architecture identifies canonical design-system sources, while direct task routing tells agents to query only matching inventory entries.

evidence.observation: The sources-of-truth table maps reusable components, shared styles, and the inventory to canonical files; AGENTS.md routes styling work to the inventory-usage instructions.

checks.label: Task-specific skills are exposed by change type
checks.interpretation: The authority file exposes one baseline implementation skill and separate conditional routes for every specialized task type.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md maps Astro, performance, accessibility, CSS, search, SEO, prose, and Context Health work to separate skills.

metrics.label: Sufficiency

checks.interpretation: The context explains the page, component, style, script, and generated-output boundaries.

checks.label: Validation and browser-test workflows are documented
checks.interpretation: The context identifies the relevant type, lint, build, Lighthouse, and Playwright checks.

checks.label: Accessibility and contrast review have actionable guidance
checks.interpretation: Semantic controls, keyboard behavior, visible focus, contrast, and automated/manual verification are all addressed.

checks.label: Performance and asset-isolation review are covered
checks.interpretation: The performance skill provides the checks needed to prove page-specific CSS and zero feature JavaScript.

evidence.observation: The skill requires static rendering, page-scoped scripts, production bundle checks, and mobile verification.

checks.label: Review scope and stop conditions are explicit
checks.interpretation: The baseline safe-change skill is sufficient to distinguish required work from unsafe assumptions and unrelated scope expansion.

evidence.observation: The safe-change skill defines implementation boundaries, a five-step workflow, and explicit stop conditions.

checks.label: Design-system pattern selection is actionable
checks.interpretation: The routed guide explains how to find a matching pattern, follow its implementation source, and preserve its accessibility constraints without loading the entire inventory.

metrics.label: Authority Clarity
metrics.interpretation: Authority is explicit for agent behavior, exact commands, protected files, validation guidance, and design-system sources.

checks.label: Protected-file authority is explicit

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md names exact command authority and three common checks, README.md retains five quick-start commands, docs/testing.md owns complete check guidance, and validate-agent-docs verifies documented script names.

checks.label: Design-system sources of truth are explicit
checks.interpretation: The context distinguishes implementation files, inventory, and human guidance.

evidence.observation: Architecture maps reusable components, shared styles, and the inventory to separate canonical files.

metrics.label: Active Context Size
metrics.interpretation: The declared effective context contains 40,135 characters (~10,034 estimated tokens).

details.estimationMethod: Estimated tokens = ceil(characters / 4). This is an approximation, not a tokenizer result.

methodology.scoreCalculation: For each agent-assessed metric, contribution = check weight × result score. Weights total 1. The displayed score is the sum of contributions. Status thresholds are healthy at 85% or higher, needs attention at 70–84.9%, and at risk below 70%.
methodology.assessmentBoundary: Check result, impact classification, interpretation, and evidence observations are agent-assessed. pnpm context:health deterministically derives contributions, metric scores, score statuses, file character counts, token estimates, size status, and the size interpretation.

tokenEstimation.note: This approximation is not a tokenizer result.

methodology.activeContextThresholds: Healthy at 24,000 estimated tokens or fewer, needs attention from 24,001 through 48,000, and at risk above 48,000. These are review bands for this report, not model context-window limits.

limitations: Semantic findings are an agent assessment of repository guidance, not a measurement of model behavior or output quality.

This report establishes significant Astro UI profile v2 as a new baseline because the effective-context selection rule and two out-of-scope checks changed materially; its scores are not directly comparable with the prior report.

The declared effective-context set contains full files initially required or directly routed for this profile. Matching inventory entries and implementation sources consulted later are task-dependent and excluded from the deterministic full-file measurement.

Active Context Size uses JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units) after UTF-8 decoding. The four-code-units-per-token estimate is deliberately simple and can differ materially from a real tokenizer.
The repository revision identifies the audited baseline commit. It does not claim to identify the later commit that contains this report.
